entries.english:
29 May 1261, Gretz. Wok von Rosenberg renews and increases the gifts made to his foundation at Hohenfurt.

In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. Since forgetfulness usually cuts short the memory of things done in time, they must be perpetuated by the protection of witnesses and writing. We, Wocho, marshal of Bohemia, make known to all who see these presents that, with the consent and express will of our wife and all our relatives on both sides, inspired by divine grace, we have piously given forever, with full right and without exception, the estates and revenues listed below to the Cistercian monastery at Hohenvurt, which we have begun to found and build anew in honor of Mary, the holy and perpetual virgin and mother of God, for the salvation and remedy of our soul and those of our ancestors and successors. We establish the lawful boundaries of the grant.

The woodland on the other side of the Wulta reaches westward to the road leading to Helfenberch and eastward across the lesser Wultawitz, including the whole meadow Zbyadel, which is to belong to the monastery. The boundary ends at the stream called Mokri; beginning at the Wulta it runs upstream to the source of that stream, then directly back over Mount Yradiss to the lesser Wultawitz, and up that stream to the height of the forest dividing Bohemia from Bavaria. On this side of the Wulta the boundary begins at the river, follows the bank called Pyzin upstream to Mount Strasedelnik, then ascends directly past the boundaries of the villages formerly belonging to Zwatemir to the boundaries of Herr Witigo de Krummenowe. We have similarly bounded the fishing rights we gave the monastery: they begin at the stream Mokry in the Wulta and extend upstream to Witigo's boundaries.

The revenues given to the monastery are the church at Rosental with all its income and a third of the tithes both from the villages we presently use and from those we have granted in fief in that parish, and the full tithes from our farm at Michenitz; the church at Predol with all its income, the full tithes from our farm at Polen, and at Zlawatitz the full crop tithes from seven ploughlands and the tithes of cheese, lambs and all else; Cedelitz near Predal, previously belonging to that church; the upper village of Gutenprunne near Strobnitz with all its income; Winthersdorf, given to the monastery through our efforts; a third of the tithes from our village Levtwinitz and a third from our village Plan.

We also acknowledge giving two vineyards, one given to us by the Graf de Hardekke and the other by our cousin Werenhard de Schowenberch der Jüngere; the newly founded and settled village of Kotzen in the land of Opava with all its rights and income; two thirds of the tithes at Sunnenberch, one third at Stradonitz and the full tithes from our farm at Malschitz; two house sites with their fields at Cedlixrevt; and Wawitz with all its income. We also gave the village Ponedraz near Wezzel with full right. In the final period of our life we gave the market town of Stradonitz, the village of Plan and the farm of Malschitz to the monastery in their entirety and with full right.

For lasting force we have had this document written and strengthened with our seal. Witnesses: Herr Heinrich and Werenhard, brothers de Schowenberch; the younger brothers Werenhard and Heinrich of the same name; Herr Budewoy and Herr Witigo de Krummenowe; Herr Gerbert; Herr Leopold; Herr Habelo; Herr Andreas; Herr Prechtilo de Ried; Konrad de Turdeling; Benata, Benysius and Budelus, burgraves de Rosenberg; and very many others. Done and given at Gretz in the year of the Lord 1261, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June.

The triangular white-wax seal, hanging from a parchment strip, is broken in two. An armed knight stands on a bridge-like pedestal, holding a large sword in his right hand against his hip and a shield with a five-petalled rose in his left; his helmet has a fan-shaped ornament. The legend reads “Sigillvm Woccon ... de ... osenberc.” See Millauer, p. 30, no. 4.

1261, without day or place. Wok von Rosenberg gives his Hohenfurt foundation the church at Wesely and the village of Ponédraž.

In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. Since forgetfulness usually cuts short the memory of deeds, they must be perpetuated by writing and witnesses. I, Wocko de Rosenberg, marshal of Bohemia, wish it to be known to all forever that, with the consent and express will of my wife Hadwig and the counsel and will of Herr Hans, venerable bishop of Prague, my compater, I have given to my foundation, the monastery of Hohenfurt, the church at Wezzel and the village of Ponedraz nearby, in full with all the revenues they may yield. It is to be known that Herr Lenco, parish priest of that church, shall have the church with one third of the tithes and compensation given from my other goods for the said village only for his lifetime. To strengthen this gift I ordered this letter written and secured it with my seal.

Witnesses: Herr Witigo de Crummenowe; Herr Albert de Borschow; Herr Billung; Herr Jakob; Herr Hirzo; Herr Hotizlaus; Herr Nicolaus; Herr Gerbert; Herr Leopold; Benisius and his brothers; and very many others. Done in the year of the Lord 1261.

The charter was damaged by insects in several places at an early date, since old copies already have the same gaps. An additional word follows “my goods”; its initial is probably d and its ending contains b, h or l with an abbreviation. The seal is as in the preceding charter, well preserved but poorly impressed, so that only the cross and “Ro” of the legend are clear. See Millauer, p. 27, no. 3.
